description.narrative: OPC-programmet i Albanien är inriktat på två huvudområden: 1) medborgardeltagande och 2) arbetstagares rättigheter. OPC samarbetar med albanska fackföreningar, organisationer för arbetstagares rättigheter och POP-nätverket (ett nätverk av 13 lokalt baserade organisationer) för att uppnå programmets huvudmål, nämligen att Albanien ska stärka kapaciteten och legitimiteten hos det civila samhällets organisationer och stödja verksamhet som säkerställer att politiska, sociala och ekonomiska processer är delaktiga. Den typ av aktiviteter som genomförs i denna insats omfattar bland annat offentliga forum med valkandidater, övervakning och förespråkande av genomförandet av sociala kontrakt på lokal nivå, drift av ett resursnav och en arbetsakademi för att stödja nya fackföreningar och fackföreningsmedlemmar, observation av kränkningar av arbetstagares rättigheter, juridisk utbildning av arbetstagare, utbyte med liknande organisationer i regionen, Kapacitetsuppbyggande verksamhet och samarbete med internationella arbetarrörelseorganisationer.

The OPC programme in Albania focuses on two main areas: 1) citizen participation and 2) labour rights. OPC partners with Albanian trade unions, labour right organisations and POP network (a network of 13 locally based organisations) to achieve the main objective of the programme and that is Albania is to the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes. The type of activities implemented in this intervention include among others public forums with elections’ candidates, monitoring and advocating for the implementation of Social Contracts at the local level, running of a resource hub and labour academy to support new trade unions and unionists, observing violations of labour rights, legal education of workers, exchange with similar organisations in the region, capacity building activities and collaboration with international labour movement organisations.

The objective of the programme is to strengthen the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes. Civil society organisations will empower citizens to claim and exercise their rights and contribute to the advancement of good governance and socio-economic rights.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution OPC Programme Albania 2023-2027

description.narrative:
The programme focuses on two thematic areas:
1) Citizens participation for democratic local governance
POP network partners supported through OPC contributed to the advancement of local democracy, civic participation, and institutional accountability across 10 municipalities. The project focused on monitoring and advocating for the implementation of the Social Contracts 2023-2027 and the Law nr 146/2014 on Notification and Public Consultation, fostering a culture of transparency and active citizen engagement in local governance. This engagement led to tangible outcomes, such as the integration of citizen priorities into municipal budgets and policies, the establishment of youth councils, and improved social inclusion plans in several municipalities.
Some concrete examples of results:
- In Tirana, the GADC (Tirana based member of POP network) has successfully influenced the Municipality to increase the Empowering Women and Promoting Entrepreneurship fund. The fund supports rural women, single mothers, and Roma women, particularly those experiencing intimate partner violence, offering € 6 000 grants for business development and a one-year exemption from municipal taxes. Additionally, beneficiaries receive mentorship and training. The GADC network has played a vital role in increasing the number of women benefiting from this support, helping them navigate the application process and access resources. Empowering women who have faced violence is essential for breaking the cycle of abuse and poverty.
- After a year of advocacy efforts from the POP partner Vlora Youth Center, the Vlora municipality council adopted a new transparency programme, a crucial step toward increased openness and accountability. The programme requires the municipality to publish information about decisions, budgets, and contact details on its website. A dedicated coordinator has been appointed and a working group of 13 civil servants established to carry out the work.
- In Puka, a designated official for public consultations and transparency was appointed, and the municipal website was updated with contact information, responsibilities, and details on accessing public information.
- The monitoring report for Vau i Dejes revealed a critical lack of published minutes from municipal council meetings, highlighting a significant transparency gap. Following recommendations, the municipality published full minutes on its official website, ensuring citizens have access to detailed records of local government activities.
2) Ensuring respect for socio-economic/labour rights
During 2024, the programme has made steps forward in strengthening the labour movement by implementing the bottom-up approach where the focus is the grassroot trade unions and embryonic movements.
Overall, the trade union partners have increased their strength and improved the connection with the member base compared to 2023, however, the capacity to organise and the effectiveness of actions is quite diverse among partners. A positive development in this regard is the significant growth and improvement in terms of membership and power of the Union of Hydrocarbon Sector. For the first time, workers at Albanias largest private oil company, Bankers Petroleum, have signed a collective agreement. In a short time, the union has successfully organised over half of the companys employees, an important breakthrough in a Chinese company where unionization has long been resisted.
A significant development in this area is also the establishment of the new federation of trade unions, called the Union of Trade Unions of Albania (UTUA). It consists mostly of new trade unions active in the sectors of oil and gas, health sector, public administration, public services, call centers, police and textile and leather sector. This initiative represents a significant shift in the trade union landscape, potentially revitalizing a movement that has been historically dominated by older confederations. The members of the federation organised a series protests and petitions and have dealt with numerous individual and collective issues related to injustices in the workplace and consolidated experience in resolving them.
OPC partners have successfully provided legal aid and other forms of assistance to workers whose labour rights have been violated, resulting in several tangible outcomes, as in receiving financial compensation for unrightful dismissal from work; increase of wages; payment of social contributions. These success cases have built trust among the members, demonstrating that their concerns are taken seriously and can be effectively addressed.
A concrete success story is the advocacy of Hydrocarbon Sector Union. For the first time, workers at Albania's largest private oil company, Bankers Petroleum, have signed a collective agreement despite resistance from the company management. When the conflict risked escalating into a strike, both parties were called to new talks by the Ministry of Economy and an agreement was finally reached. The agreement includes wage increases for 200 of the lowest-paid workers, a doubled meal allowance, and the right to renegotiate wages annually which are major steps toward better working conditions.
